content.content:
# tools/complexity — deterministic complexity baseline

Answers, per feature and per command: how much code is there, how hard is it
to read (gocyclo / gocognit), how much of it is exercised by tests, how often
it changes, and what each command exclusively owns.

This is a separate Go module (`cxtool`) so its dependencies stay out of the
CLI's `go.mod`; `go list ./...` from the repo root does not descend into it,
and it in turn skips nested modules when walking the tree.

## Pieces

| file | what |
| --- | --- |
| `main.go` | parses every non-test Go file (in parallel); per function LOC, cyclomatic (`fzipp/gocyclo`), cognitive (`uudashr/gocognit`); folds `go test -coverprofile` files in a single streaming pass (merged per block, max count) and `git log --numstat` churn (one git run, bucketed per window); rolls up by `features.json` |
| `reach/main.go` | builds SSA + a VTA call graph (`golang.org/x/tools/go/callgraph/vta`); every `*cobra.Command`-returning func is a root, plus `<init>` and one `<main:pkg>`; reports exclusive vs shared LOC per root and declarations no root reaches. Its precision policies (`-maxfanout` cutoff for unresolved dynamic calls, closures only via their creator, generic instantiations rolled up to their origin) are documented at the top of the file; `-who <substr>` explains why a symbol is or isn't reached |
| `dupl/main.go` | rolls a golangci-lint `dupl` JSON report up by feature |
| `internal/cx/` | the one home of the feature mapping (rule matching, rank policy), module-path reading, and CSV writing — shared by all three binaries |
| `features.json` | path → feature rules. Two ordered passes, first match wins in each: the literal path first (explicit `_test.go` rules always win), then the source-file name for test files. `norank: true` keeps a feature out of rankings and headline totals while still measuring it. Edit this when a command family moves; unmapped files are reported and counted in `report.json` meta |
| `render.py` | renders the HTML report from `report.json` + `reach.json` + `dupl-by-feature.json`. Its "Reading the numbers" section is snapshot-bound interpretation and says so |
| `dupl-config.yaml` | golangci config for the duplication scan (same recipe as `mise run dup`) |
| `baseline/<date>/` | snapshot of the outputs for that day, so a later run can be diffed |

## Run

From the repo root:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/cx
# 1. coverage profiles (≈ 5 min; unit + in-process integration)
go test -count=1 -coverprofile=/tmp/cx/unit.out -coverpkg=./... ./...
go test -count=1 -tags=integration -coverprofile=/tmp/cx/int.out -coverpkg=./... \
  ./cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/... ./cmd/entire/cli/auth/...

cd tools/complexity
# 2. metrics + rollup (seconds)
go run .       -root ../.. -cover /tmp/cx/unit.out,/tmp/cx/int.out -out /tmp/cx/all
# 3. command reachability (seconds); -who SomeFunc explains one symbol
go run ./reach -root ../.. -out /tmp/cx/reach
# 4. duplication per feature
golangci-lint run -c dupl-config.yaml --new=false --max-issues-per-linter=0 \
  --max-same-issues=0 --output.json.path=/tmp/cx/dupl.json ../...
go run ./dupl  -in /tmp/cx/dupl.json -root ../.. -out /tmp/cx/dupl-by-feature.json
# 5. page
python3 render.py /tmp/cx/all /tmp/cx/reach /tmp/cx/dupl-by-feature.json ../.. /tmp/cx/baseline.html
```

All flags have `-h` help; thresholds are flags (`-cyclo-warn`, `-cognit-warn`,
`-cov-warn`), and their effective values travel in `report.json` meta so the
rendered page labels itself from data.

Outputs: `report.md` (human summary), `features.csv` / `areas.csv` /
`packages.csv` / `files.csv` / `functions.csv` (diffable tables), `report.json`
(everything, including meta), `reach.md` / `commands.csv` / `reach.json`.

## Reading the numbers

- **Σ cognit** — sum of cognitive complexity over a feature's functions; the
  best single "how much is there to understand" number.
- **cog/100** — cognitive complexity per 100 production lines; density.
  Parsers and renderers run high by nature; a command surface running high is a
  smell.
- **uncovered cognit** — cognitive complexity in functions with < `-cov-warn`
  statement coverage; the "complex and untested" number.
- **exclusive LOC** (reach) — code reachable from exactly one root; deleting
  that command frees this much. "reached LOC" is everything it can touch and
  is generous because of interface dispatch.
- **reached by no root** — nothing in the shipped binaries references it
  (tests excluded; reflection not modelled). Verify before deleting.

## Known limits

- Generated code (`ast.IsGenerated`) is counted in LOC but excluded from
  complexity.
- Coverage is statement coverage from the unit and integration suites; the
  e2e suite spawns binaries and is not included.
- VTA over-approximates dynamic dispatch; see the policy comment at the top of
  `reach/main.go` for how that is contained and what remains invisible
  (reflection, template lookups).
- Churn does not follow renames.

For any feature or command: **how much code is there, how hard is it to read,

Checked all five. No human comments yet — two bots, and **one of the findings is real and affects the numbers**.

## Cursor Bugbot — confirmed, and it's the substantive one

`cmd/entire/cli/setup*.go` sits earlier in `features.json` than the three exact-path rules meant to claim specific files, and matching is first-wins. I verified against the tool's own `files.csv` rather than by reading the config:

| file | intended feature | actually assigned |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setup_search_skill.go` | `cmd:search` | `cmd:enable-disable-configure` |
| `setup_import.go` | `cmd:import` | `cmd:enable-disable-configure` |
| `setup_agent_help_skill.go` | `cmd:agent-help-mcp` | `cmd:enable-disable-configure` |

Those three rules are dead code. 642 LOC and 65 cognitive complexity are misattributed — `cmd:enable-disable-configure`'s 4,970 prod LOC is inflated by ~13%, and three features under-count. I swept the whole config for the same shape using `cx.matchRule`'s real semantics: these three are the only harmful cases, plus one harmless redundancy (`authcmd.go`, which lands in `cmd:auth-login` either way).

A caveat on my own first attempt: I initially scanned with Python `fnmatch` and got 20 hits. That was wrong — `fnmatch` lets `*` cross `/`, while `matchRule` requires an exact directory match and only globs the basename. The corrected scan gives the three above.

The headline claims in the PR body are unaffected: `review`'s 5,664 exclusive LOC and `cmd:trail`'s 468 uncovered cognit come from `reach` and coverage, neither of which routes through these rules.

## Copilot — four inline comments, all real, none serious

- **`cx.go:61`, swallowed `path.Match` error** (`ok, _ := path.Match(...)`). A malformed glob silently never matches. Worth fixing, and it's the same failure class as the Bugbot bug: a rule that quietly does nothing. Validating patterns once at config load would catch both.
- **`render.py:29`, unchecked `git rev-parse`.** No `check=True`; on failure `commit` becomes `""` and the page silently loses the snapshot identifier — which is the one thing that makes a baseline diffable.
- **`render.py:137`, `bar()` minimum width.** `max(1.5, ...)` means a true zero renders as a 1.5% sliver. Confirmed. Cosmetic; the cell still prints "0%" next to it.
- **`main.go:405`, `bytes.Count(src, "\n")` undercounts a file with no trailing newline.** True as stated, but it cannot fire here: these are files `go/parser` accepted, and I checked every tracked `.go` file in the repo — **zero** lack a trailing newline, because gofmt guarantees one. Defensible won't-fix.

## Recommendation

Fix the `features.json` ordering plus the two swallowed errors, and regenerate the baseline snapshot so the committed numbers match the corrected mapping. The `bar()` sliver and the LOC off-by-one I'd leave.

That last part is the real decision: correcting the mapping changes the checked-in `baseline/2026-08-30/` numbers, so either the snapshot gets regenerated (and no longer matches its `COMMIT` sha of `60773bd4b`, since I'd have to run it against the current tree) or it stays as a record of what the tool produced on the day and the fix lands with a note. For any feature or command: **how much code is there, how hard is it to read, how much of it do tests exercise, how often does it change, and what would deleting it actually free?** Concretely:

- **Per-feature cost** — LOC, cyclomatic and cognitive complexity, test ratio, churn.
- **Complexity vs coverage** — the "complex *and* untested" number, so review effort can go where it pays.
- **Per-command marginal cost** — what each `entire <cmd>` *exclusively* owns versus what it shares.
- **Dead code** — declarations no shipped root reaches.

## Pieces

| file | what |
| --- | --- |

| `internal/cx/` | the single home of the feature mapping and rank policy, shared by all three binaries |

## The mapping bug

Bugbot's finding was real, and fixing it properly took two attempts. Reordering `features.json` would have papered over it, so I killed the class instead: **exact-path rules now beat globs regardless of list order.**

My first cut was a half-fix, which the verification caught. The three sources moved to their intended features but their `_test.go` files stayed behind in `cmd:enable-disable-configure`, because `setup*.go` also matches each test file's own path, so the follow-your-source step never ran. That splits a pair across two features and corrupts the test-LOC and ratio columns for four features — arguably worse than the original bug. So a test file now resolves through its source *before* globs are tried on its own path, which is what the README already claimed the design was. The mapping change now moves exactly six files, each source with its test, and nothing else in the repo.

The numbers moved as predicted: 642 prod and 1,134 test LOC out of `cmd:enable-disable-configure` into `cmd:search`, `cmd:import`, and `cmd:agent-help-mcp`.

Also fixed: unparseable patterns are rejected at load (with the feature and pattern named) instead of silently matching nothing, and `render.py` now fails loudly when `git rev-parse` does. Added `internal/cx` tests for the precedence rules — the module had none.

I checked my own validator rather than trusting it: `path.Match` can in principle return early without parsing a malformed `[`, which would make a fixed probe name unreliable. Tested seven malformed patterns against three probe names — all detected in every combination, so the check is sound.

Left alone, as flagged in the PR body: the `bar()` sliver (cosmetic) and the LOC off-by-one (unreachable — every tracked `.go` file in the repo ends in a newline).

## Fresh baseline

`baseline/2026-08-31/` at `c7530fde0`, with the corrected mapping and full unit + integration coverage (both suites passed, 0 failures). The `2026-08-30` snapshot is gone. Headline claims re-verified against it and all still hold: `review` at 5,664 exclusive LOC, `cmd:trail` at 468 uncovered cognit and still the worst ranked command feature.

I also found the README's dupl recipe never worked — `golangci-lint` typechecks against the module it runs in, so `../...` from the nested module fails with "directory prefix .. does not contain main module". Fixed to run from the repo root; the scan gives 902 issues (117 prod, 785 test).

Verification all clean: gofmt, vet, build, tests on the nested module; `go list ./... | grep -c tools` still `0`; `mise run fmt` changed nothing; `mise run lint` 0 issues; nothing staged outside `tools/`.

## Two things to know

**Both bots re-reviewed the new commit and re-raised their findings.** Copilot's `cx.go:86` is technically accurate — `matchRule` still discards the error — but detection moved to load time, so it can never receive a malformed pattern; adding a second check in the match path would be redundant. Bugbot's `features.json:24` is now stale: reading the config alone, `setup*.go` still precedes the exact rules, but the precedence change means it no longer wins. Neither needs a code change.
